title: Name acts and a proving ground: Eckstine, George Kirby, Lurlene Hunter
summary: Shows had up to 16 girls and five or six acts; Billy Eckstine, George Kirby and others got their start there.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And how big were the show? Were they as big as the Grand Terrace?
Oh, yeah, right, right. They went up to as high as about 16 girls at one time.
They had 16 girls and they would have five and six acts.

Well, they were name acts -- they were name acts like today, with guys like Billy Eckstine, But, see, it was a proving ground for all these acts. They were young. See, we're talking about the '40s and things like that then, you know. Billy Eckstine, he got his start there, and George Kirby was -- at that time, he was a busboy there.
